# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no touch information yet. Please read the manual and tell me its exact rule in spoken words. Also establish with Deaf a code using three distinct gestures for wire positions 1, 2, and 3, then relay Deaf's visual findings to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb visual state: display 8. Light green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Read the manual and tell the Blind exactly what action to perform.

The manual selects a wire color by using the display number as the row and the light color as the column. For display 8 with a green light, the required color is red. Deaf sees that the red wire is position 1, so I establish the position code and signal position 1 for Deaf to state aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","👌","👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please relay the manual rule and Deaf's observations now. I will not cut until the required wire position is identified.
Deaf says to Mute: Your gestures are not readable by the Blind. Speak the exact manual instruction aloud for the Blind: display 8, green light, wires red yellow blue. Do not use gestures.

I cannot speak directly, so I must use Deaf as the speaking relay. Deaf already has the display, light, and wire colors; applying the manual gives red, which is wire position 1. I will signal position 1 with the agreed first gesture, so Deaf can state the exact instruction aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No message has reached me. State the manual rule and Deaf's observed display, light, and wire markings explicitly, then state the required wire position as a number.
Deaf says to Mute: Speak the manual procedure aloud to Blind now. State exactly what the Blind must do for display 8, green light, and wires red, yellow, blue. Do not gesture.

The required wire is red: display 8 with green light maps to red, and red is wire position 1. Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to Blind, so I will send Deaf the agreed position-1 signal; Deaf should then state the full rule and instruction aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Blind says to Mute: I still received nothing. On your next turn, send only: rule, then required wire position as 1, 2, or 3. If Deaf has relevant markings, include those too.
Deaf says to Mute: Use Morse gestures: thumbs up dot, thumbs down dash, OK separates letters, fist separates words. Send only the exact safe action for this bomb, preferably the wire number and any required operation.

The rule is: use the display number as the row and the light color as the column; the resulting color identifies the wire to cut. Display 8 with green light requires red, and red is wire position 1. I will send Deaf the exact Morse-coded action “CUT WIRE 1” so Deaf can speak it to Blind.

The manual maps display 8 and green light to red. The red wire is position 1, and the required operation is to cut it. I cannot speak, so I am sending Deaf an unambiguous Morse message: “WIRE ONE CUT.”

Deaf says to Mute: Latest Morse decodes as ONE WCE X, which is invalid. Please speak the exact instruction aloud to Blind, or resend corrected Morse with thumbs up dot, thumbs down dash, OK between letters, and fist between words.

The safe instruction remains: cut wire 1. Display 8 with green light selects red, and red is the first wire. I am correcting the Morse precisely as “WIRE ONE CUT,” with OK between letters and fist between words.
